items.actClause: AN ACT to amend the public health law, in relation to nominations to board of visitors for state veterans' homes
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER:  S6144

 TITLE OF BILL :  An act to amend the public health law, in relation
to nominations to board of visitors for state veterans' homes

 PURPOSE :

This bill requires that vacancies on the state veterans' homes board
of visitors be filled in a timely fashion.

 SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS :

Section One amends section 2631 of the public health law, by requiring
that a vacancy on the board of visitors for state operated veteran
homes be filled within ninety days of a vacancy occurring.

Section Two provides that this act shall take effect immediately.

 EXISTING LAW :

New Legislation

 JUSTIFICATION :

The board of visitors plays an important role in the operation of
state run veterans' homes. They serve as ambassadors to the homes,
monitor the way the home is administered (independent of DOH), recruit
residents through presentations to local veteran organizations,
solicit funds through contributions from veterans' organizations,
participate in monthly Resident Council meetings, finance and arrange
off site activities and are present within the facility for the
purpose of receiving feedback from staff and residents.

Unfortunately, the boards currently have an overwhelming number of
vacancies. The Governor has not appointed any new members to the board
of visitors since he took office in 2011. Further, statute provides
that a members' term shall be for a period of five years.  Since the
Governor has not reappointed any past members since he took office,
all current members are serving in a holdover capacity. It has been
reported to the Legislature that several candidates for appointment
withdrew their names from consideration, after waiting over three
years, with no action by the Governor. It has also been reported to
the legislature that two of the homes are unable to function, as they
no longer have enough members to form a quorum.

Despite this issue being raised with the Governor's Office over a year
ago, prolonged vacancies continue to interrupt the functions of this
governing board. By requiring that a nomination be put forward within
ninety days of a vacancy occurring, we can ensure that these boards
are able to function and carry out their important responsibilities.

 LEGISLATIVE HISTORY :

New Bill.

 FISCAL IMPLICATIONS :

None to the State.

 EFFECTIVE DATE :
This bill shall take effect immediately.

Visitors be filled in a timely fashion.

for the appointment of interim members by the current board, in the
event that a vacancy is not filled within 270 days of occurring.

Section Two provides that this act shall take effect immediately.

New Legislation

The Board of Visitors plays an important role in the operation of state
run veterans' homes. They serve as ambassadors to the homes, monitor the
way the home is administered (independent of DOH), recruit residents
through presentations to local veteran organizations, solicit funds
through contributions from veterans' organizations, participate in
monthly Resident Council meetings, finance and arrange off site activ-
ities and are present within the facility for the purpose of receiving
feedback from staff and residents.

Unfortunately, the boards currently have an overwhelming number of
vacancies. The Governor has not appointed any new members to the Board
of Visitors since he took office in 2011. Further, statute provides that
a members' term shall be for a period of five years.  Since the Governor
has not reappointed any past members since he took office, all current
members are serving in a holdover capacity. It has been reported to the
Legislature that several candidates for appointment withdrew their names
from consideration, after waiting over three years, with no action by
the Governor. It has also been reported to the legislature that two of
the homes are unable to function, as they no longer have enough members
to form a quorum.

Despite this issue being raised with the Governor's Office over a year
ago, prolonged vacancies continue to interrupt the functions of this
governing board. By allowing the board to appoint interim members in the
event that a nomination is not made by the Governor in a timely fashion,
we can ensure that these boards are able to function and carry out their
important responsibilities.

New Bill.

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

None to the State.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This bill shall take effect immediately.

items.memoText:
VETO MESSAGE - No. 264
 
TO THE SENATE:
 
I am returning herewith, without my approval, the following bill:
 
Senate Bill Number 6144-B, entitled:
 
    "AN  ACT  to  amend  the  public  health law, in relation to filling
      vacancies on a board of visitors for state veterans' homes"
 
    NOT APPROVED
 
  This bill would authorize the temporary appointment of a member  to  a
board  of  visitors  for  state  veterans' homes. The bill would allow a
majority vote of the current active and hold-over members to appoint the
temporary member.
 
  Under the current law, the Governor selects  members  to  serve  on  a
board  of visitors for state veterans' homes with the advice and consent
of the Senate. The law also requires that these members be  chosen  from
the  New  York departments of the major organizations of war veterans or
their women's auxiliaries. When selecting  members  to  serve  on  these
boards,  my office conducts a thorough background check in an attempt to
ensure the good character of these appointees.  This  bill  attempts  to
establish  a  new  process  to fill temporary vacancies on these boards.
While the intent of the bill is worthy, the  bill  contains  significant
flaws that prevent me from signing it into law.
 
  First, the bill, unlike the current law, does not require an appointee
to  be  a  member  of  any of the major organizations of war veterans or
their women's auxiliaries. Additionally, the bill does not  provide  any
assurance that these temporary appointees are properly vetted to protect
the  health  and  safety  of the residents of the veterans' homes. Board
members' roles include  monitoring  the  administration  of  the  homes,
interacting with local veterans organizations, soliciting contributions,
participating in meetings, and arranging off-site activities. The health
and  safety of the men and women who bravely put their lives on the line
to defend this country are of the utmost concern to me and  my  adminis-
tration,  and  allowing  inadequate  vetting  of  board  members who are
frequently present in the homes is unacceptable.
 
  Second, this bill would establish an unclear appointment  process  and
could result in unintended consequences. The bill requires that a major-
ity  of  the  current and hold-over members vote on proposed appointees.
However, the bill does not  set  forth  any  nomination  procedures.  As
drafted,  any  person,  including  non-board  members,  could nominate a
potential appointee. Further, while the worthwhile goal of the  bill  is
to  temporarily  appoint  board members while a permanent appointment is
pending, were the Senate to simply refuse to take up a Governor's  nomi-
nation,  a  temporary  member  could  become a de facto permanent member
without any of the term limits provided under the current law.  For  the
foregoing reasons, I am constrained to veto this bill.
 
  The bill is disapproved.                    (signed) ANDREW M. CUOMO
 
                               __________
